verdict.rationale: Apple's own M4 Max announcement says developers can interact with LLMs of nearly 200 billion parameters, which covers 70B-class quantized models with room to spare. The spec sheet publishes 546GB/s of memory bandwidth, and Apple's MLX framework runs on unified memory with no data transfers between devices. Missing for 10: an explicit maximum unified-memory capacity figure for M4 Max in the evidence, and independent hands-on benchmarks of 70B-class inference speed.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run a large local LLM (70B-class, quantized) on this platform — enough addressable memory and published memory bandwidth to make local inference practical

citations.quote: This allows developers to easily interact with large language models that have nearly 200 billion parameters.
M4 Max with 16-core CPU and 40-core GPU (546GB/s memory bandwidth)
over half a terabyte per second of unified memory bandwidth, and a Neural Engine that is over 3x faster than M1 Max, Mac Studio with M4 Max can run on-device AI models incredibly fast.
Arrays in MLX live in shared memory. Operations on MLX arrays can be performed on any of the supported device types without transferring data.
